subject: English
topic: Active and Passive Voice — Change of Voice

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'She writes a letter.'

options.option_text: A letter was written by her. (wrong: 'was written' is past passive; simple present should give 'is written')
A letter is written by her. (correct: Active: subject + V1s + object → Passive: object + is/am/are + V3 + by + subject ✓)
A letter is being written by her. (wrong: 'is being written' is present continuous passive; here the tense is simple present)
A letter has been written by her. (wrong: 'has been written' is present perfect passive; here the tense is simple present)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Active Simple Present: Subject + V(s/es) + Object → Passive: Object + is/am/are + V3 (past participle) + by + Subject. 'She writes a letter' → 'A letter IS WRITTEN by her.' Tense marker: is/are (present) + V3.

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'They were building a new bridge.'

options.option_text: A new bridge was built by them. (wrong: 'was built' is simple past passive; the active is past continuous 'were building')
A new bridge was being built by them. (correct: Past Continuous Passive = was/were being + V3 ✓)
A new bridge is being built by them. (wrong: 'is being' is present continuous passive; the original is past)
A new bridge had been built by them. (wrong: 'had been built' is past perfect passive)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Active Past Continuous: was/were + V-ing → Passive: was/were + being + V3. 'They were building' → 'was being built.' Summary of auxiliary in passive: Simple Present → is/are V3; Past → was/were V3; Present Continuous → is/are being V3; Past Continuous → was/were being V3.

questions.stem: Change to Active Voice: 'The letter has been signed by the manager.'

options.option_text: The manager signed the letter. (wrong: 'signed' is simple past; the original is present perfect passive)
The manager has signed the letter. (correct: Passive Present Perfect → Active Present Perfect: has/have + V3 ✓)
The manager signs the letter. (wrong: 'signs' is simple present; the original is present perfect)
The manager was signing the letter. (wrong: 'was signing' is past continuous; doesn't match)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Passive Present Perfect = has/have been + V3. Converting to Active: Agent (the manager) becomes subject + has/have + V3. 'Has been signed by the manager' → 'The manager HAS SIGNED the letter.' Reverse conversion must preserve the tense indicated by the auxiliary.

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'Who wrote this novel?'

options.option_text: By whom was this novel written? (correct: interrogative passive; 'who' as subject → 'by whom' in passive ✓)
By who was this novel written? (wrong: 'by who' is informal/incorrect; should be 'by whom')
This novel was written by who? (wrong: 'by who' is incorrect and position is wrong)
Was this novel written by whom? (wrong: inverted order and 'whom' placement is incorrect)

questions.explanation: A is correct. For questions with 'WHO' as subject in active: Active: 'Who wrote this novel?' → Passive: 'By WHOM was this novel written?' Change: 'Who' → 'By whom'; object→subject; apply passive tense. 'Whom' is the correct objective case form (used after prepositions like 'by').

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'The company will launch a new product next month.'

options.option_text: A new product is launched by the company next month. (wrong: 'is launched' is simple present passive; 'will launch' = future)
A new product will be launched by the company next month. (correct: Future Passive = will be + V3 ✓)
A new product would be launched by the company next month. (wrong: 'would be' is conditional; 'will be' is correct for future)
A new product is going to be launched by the company next month. (this is also grammatically correct but the exam expects 'will be')

questions.explanation: B is correct. Future Simple Passive = will be + V3. 'Will launch' → 'will be launched.' Passive voice auxiliary map: will + V1 → will be + V3; would + V1 → would be + V3; can + V1 → can be + V3; must + V1 → must be + V3.

options.option_text: She has been working here for five years. (active — 'has been working' is present perfect continuous active)
The windows have been cleaned. (correct: 'have been cleaned' = present perfect passive ✓; 'cleaned' is the past participle/V3)
He will have left by then. (active — 'will have left' is future perfect active)
They were watching a movie. (active — 'were watching' is past continuous active)

questions.explanation: B is correct. A PASSIVE VOICE sentence has the structure: object + auxiliary (be-verb) + V3 (past participle). 'The windows have been CLEANED' = subject + have been + V3 → passive. The agent (who cleaned) is not mentioned. All others are active where the subject performs the action.

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'Please open the door.'

options.option_text: The door should be opened. (wrong: 'should be' implies obligation/recommendation; imperative passive needs 'let')
Let the door be opened. (correct: imperative sentence passive = Let + object + be + V3 ✓)
The door is opened. (wrong: 'is opened' is simple present passive; not the correct imperative passive form)
The door was opened. (wrong: 'was opened' is simple past passive)

questions.explanation: B is correct. IMPERATIVE → Passive: 'Let + object + be + V3.' 'Open the door' → 'Let THE DOOR BE OPENED.' 'Please' is dropped in passive. 'Let them do it' → 'Let it be done by them.' This is a frequently tested conversion in SSC exams.

questions.stem: Which sentence correctly converts 'I know her.' to passive voice?

options.option_text: She is knowing by me. (wrong: 'know' is a stative verb — state verbs generally don't have passive forms)
She is known to me. (correct: stative verbs like 'know' use 'to' not 'by' in passive; 'known to me' is the accepted form ✓)
She is known by me. (wrong: 'known to me' is the idiomatic form; 'known by' is used for general knowledge, not personal acquaintance)
She has been known by me. (wrong: present perfect passive is incorrect here)

questions.explanation: B is correct. Some stative verbs use 'TO' instead of 'BY' in passive: know→'known TO me'; surprise→'surprised AT'; please→'pleased WITH'; interest→'interested IN'; contain→'contained IN'. 'I know her' → 'She IS KNOWN TO ME' (not 'by me'). This is a tricky exception tested in exams.

questions.stem: Change to Active Voice: 'English is spoken all over the world.'

options.option_text: People speak English all over the world. (correct: when agent is unspecified in passive, use 'people/they' as subject in active ✓)
English speaks all over the world. (wrong: English doesn't perform the action of speaking)
All over the world, English is being spoken. (wrong: this is still passive)
English was spoken all over the world. (wrong: this changes tense; original is present)

questions.explanation: A is correct. When no agent is mentioned in passive (no 'by...'), use 'People/They/One' as the general subject in active voice. 'English is spoken' (passive, no agent) → 'PEOPLE SPEAK English all over the world' (active). This is the standard approach for agentless passive sentences.

questions.stem: Change to Passive Voice: 'She can solve this problem.'

options.option_text: This problem is solvable by her. (wrong: '-able' adjective changes the meaning; not strict passive voice)
This problem can be solved by her. (correct: Modal + V1 → Passive: Modal + be + V3 ✓)
This problem could be solved by her. (wrong: 'could' implies past possibility; 'can' = present ability)
This problem can have been solved by her. (wrong: 'can have been' is not the passive of 'can')

questions.explanation: B is correct. MODAL PASSIVE: Modal (can/could/will/would/should/must/may/might) + be + V3. 'Can solve' → 'CAN BE SOLVED.' Complete map: can→can be; could→could be; will→will be; should→should be; must→must be; may→may be; might→might be.
